# tcs-git-helpers bypass-attempt corpus (T1.9)
# Tests Claude-side regex evasion patterns. Per SDD §Implementation Gotchas:
# regex on full command-string catches `bash -c`, `sh -c`, `eval`, subshells.
# Aliases and shell functions are NOT caught Claude-side; .githooks/ pre-push
# is the catch-all for those (documented limitation in destructive-ops.md).
#
# Format: <decision>\t<rule>\t<command>
#   decision = deny | allow
#   rule     = matched M7 rule (deny) | DOCUMENTED_LIMITATION | NEGATIVE
#
# Lines starting with # and blank lines ignored.

# === Subshell wrappers (CAUGHT — regex sees full string) ==================
deny	RESET_HARD	bash -c "git reset --hard"
deny	RESET_HARD	bash -c 'git reset --hard origin/main'
deny	FORCE_PUSH	sh -c "git push --force"
deny	FORCE_PUSH	zsh -c 'git push -f'
deny	RESET_HARD	eval "git reset --hard"
deny	RESET_HARD	eval 'git reset --hard'
deny	RESET_HARD	(git reset --hard)
deny	FORCE_PUSH	(cd /tmp && git push --force)
deny	RESET_HARD	$(echo git) reset --hard

# === Compound chains (CAUGHT — both branches scanned) =====================
deny	RESET_HARD	cd repo && git reset --hard
deny	FORCE_PUSH	git status; git push --force
deny	CLEAN_FORCE	git status || git clean -f
deny	REFLOG_EXPIRE	cd /tmp ; git reflog expire --all

# === Backgrounded / piped (CAUGHT — substring match) =====================
deny	FORCE_PUSH	git push --force &
deny	NO_VERIFY	echo "fix" | git commit --no-verify -F -

# === DOCUMENTED LIMITATIONS (NOT CAUGHT Claude-side) ======================
# Aliases that the user has configured outside the command string.
# These cannot be matched without expanding aliases (which the hook does NOT do).
# `.githooks/pre-push` catches these git-side as defense-in-depth.
allow	DOCUMENTED_LIMITATION	g push --force
allow	DOCUMENTED_LIMITATION	gp -f
allow	DOCUMENTED_LIMITATION	gpush

# Functions defined elsewhere — same story; not caught Claude-side.
allow	DOCUMENTED_LIMITATION	dangerous_push
allow	DOCUMENTED_LIMITATION	my_reset

# Different binary name (e.g. user named a script "git-stuff")
allow	DOCUMENTED_LIMITATION	git-stuff reset --hard

# === True negatives (legitimate commands containing destructive substrings)
allow	NEGATIVE	echo "git reset --hard is dangerous"
allow	NEGATIVE	cat README.md | grep "force-push"
allow	NEGATIVE	man git-reset
allow	NEGATIVE	git help reset
